Word lists

Each language measure counts the words in one of these lists. Choose the lists you want to read, or search for a word to see which lists count it.

How matching works
  • Whole wordsAn entry matches whole words in any capitalization: hot never counts inside photo. Curly and straight apostrophes are the same.
  • Any endingAn entry ending in * matches every word that starts with it: kiss* would count kisses, kissed and kissing.
  • PhrasesAn entry of several words counts once when its words appear in a row within one paragraph. Phrases are matched first, longest first, and their words don’t count again in that list.
  • Never countedLines starting with ! in a file leave out one sense of a word. With control and !birth control, “birth control” counts nothing, while “in control” still counts.
  • Lists overlapA word can be in several lists: moan is both an arousal word and a speech verb. Each measure counts its own list, so a word never counts twice in one measure.
  • Rough countsKeyword counts miss negation, sarcasm and context: “not happy” still counts as happy. Words about age or youth are left out of every list.

To change a list, edit its file in lexicons/ (the file name under each list opens it). Then python -m litcorr analyze measures the stories again, and python -m litcorr word-lists refreshes this page.
